title: Redirect Trilogy
story: Every Linux process has three standard streams: `stdin` (0), `stdout` (1), and `stderr` (2). Noisy programs often mix status messages and decoys across `stdout` and `stderr`. Control where each stream goes to isolate the signal from the noise.
description:
Complete all three stages, then run `quest check`:
1. Stage 1: Run `/challenge/run` so its standard output (`stdout`) is saved into `~/myflag` while error/status messages still appear on your terminal.
2. Stage 2: Run `/challenge/run --part1` to save the first half into `~/twopart.txt`, then run `/challenge/run --part2` and **append** the second half to `~/twopart.txt` without erasing the first.
3. Stage 3: `/challenge/run2` prints decoy lines on `stdout` and the real Stage 3 token on `stderr`. Save **only** `stderr` into `~/stderr_flag.txt` while discarding `stdout`.
hints: Use standard output redirection to overwrite a file in Stage 1, and append redirection on the second command in Stage 2.
Stream `2` is `stderr`. Redirect stream `2` to `~/stderr_flag.txt` and send stream `1` (`stdout`) to `/dev/null`.
Once `~/myflag`, `~/twopart.txt`, and `~/stderr_flag.txt` are ready, run `quest check`.
